children: New listings of U.S. homes for sale rose 2.1% from a week earlier, Redfin says. That's their highest level in four years. The total number of homes for sale also ticked up. Active listings rose 0.4% week-over-week in welcome news for house hunters, who increasingly have more options and negotiating power. But demand isn't matching the uptick in supply. Pending home sales were essentially flat from a week earlier, dipping to their lowest level since February. High housing costs are the biggest hurdle for prospective buyers. The typical U.S. home-sale price rose 2.2% year-over-year, while the average weekly mortgage rate was 6.66%, near its highest level in the last year. But median U.S. asking price inched down 0.1%, a sign that sellers may be adjusting their expectations as buyers negotiate and push back against high costs. (chris.wack@wsj.com)
